question: When a non-compliant traffic control device is replaced because it is damaged, missing, or no longer serviceable, what is the general rule and the limited replacement-in-kind exception?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The general rule is that a non-compliant device being replaced or refurbished because it is damaged, missing, or no longer serviceable must be replaced with a compliant device. The rule itself points to a limited exception "as provided for in Paragraph 13 of this Section," but the text of Paragraph 13 (the replacement-in-kind exception) is not included in the evidence, so its specific terms cannot be stated here. Standards (mandatory): - "A non-compliant traffic control device that is being replaced or refurbished because it is damaged, missing, or no longer serviceable (see definition in Section 1C.02) for any reason shall be replaced with a compliant device, except as provided for in Paragraph 13 of this Section." - "Unless a particular device is no longer serviceable (see definition in Section 1C.02), non-compliant devices on existing highways and bikeways shall be brought into compliance with the current edition of the National MUTCD as part of the systematic upgrading of substandard traffic control devices (and installation of new required traffic control devices) required pursuant to the Highway Safety Program, 23 U.S.C. §402(a)." - For Federal-aid projects involving new construction, reconstruction, resurfacing, restoration, or rehabilitation, "the traffic control devices installed (temporary or permanent) shall comply with the most recent edition of the National MUTCD before that highway is opened or re-opened to the public for unrestricted travel [23 CFR 655.603(d)(2) and (d)(3)]." Options (permitted): - The evidence provided does not include the text of Paragraph 13 of Section 1B.03, which contains the limited replacement-in-kind exception; its specific conditions cannot be quoted from the available evidence. Citations: - Section 1B.03 Standard §12 (p.6) - Section 1B.03 Standard §5 (p.5) - Section 1B.03 Standard §4 (p.5)
gold_answer: The replacement must generally be a compliant device. A non-compliant device may be replaced in kind only when engineering judgment finds that a lone compliant device among adjacent non-compliant devices would confuse users and/or the planned replacement schedule for the whole series will achieve timely compliance.
